answer: In a reef-monitoring market near a river delta, let agents earn reputation only from completed jobs purchased by independently audited customers. Charge a nonrefundable settlement fee and cap reputation gained from any one customer. A swarm buying its own fake jobs must repeatedly pay fees and obtain distinct audited buyers; free aliases alone earn no standing. Treat reputation as evidence, not a fable of guaranteed honesty: colluding real customers can still launder it, and auditing can exclude newcomers.
